findings.title: Permitted executable hashes are absent from the stable execution freeze and live continuity comparison
evidence: The corrected design lists permitted controller executable file identities and hashes as stable pre-restart fields.
The frozen policy execution-freeze schema has no permitted executable identity-and-hash allowlist.
Each raw process row and observer identity contains executable_identity but no executable_sha256.
The prepare-to-publish continuity projection therefore cannot bind or compare executable SHA-256.
findings.adversarial_consequence: A same-name or same-identity executable whose bytes differ from the reviewed pre-restart executable can satisfy the current pure-policy relation if the caller supplies otherwise internally consistent raw rows.
findings.required_repair: In a new frozen generation, bind a sorted closed permitted-executable table containing normalized name, executable file identity, and SHA-256; include executable SHA-256 in raw process and observer identities; require exact direct-chain membership; and compare it across prepare and publish.

findings.title: The model-root parent token is not related to the frozen model-root identity
evidence: The policy requires canonical parent rows to be pairwise distinct.
A target or sentinel whose parent_token is the logical model-root token may reference a separate canonical-parent identity.
No invariant requires that logical model-root parent identity to equal volume_allowlist.model_identity.
findings.adversarial_consequence: A self-consistent raw and frozen tuple may place logical model-root children under a distinct same-volume directory while still passing token and parent-ID checks.
findings.required_repair: Represent the model root as an explicit root identity relation and require every model-root parent token to resolve to the exact frozen model_identity. Require every other canonical parent to be derived beneath that retained model handle and prevent inappropriate root aliases.

findings.title: The native helper observes direct ancestry but does not produce an exhaustive bounded-process inventory
evidence: Its process snapshot is used to walk ancestry, not to open, classify, and retain every bounded-name process row.
The frozen draft accurately labels this helper test-only and gives it no production provenance.
findings.adversarial_consequence: Reusing this helper as a production collector would allow an unrelated bounded writer to remain absent from the policy input.
findings.required_repair: Keep the current helper test-only. Any later production collector must enumerate the full process snapshot, classify every code-fixed bounded-name row, open and retain each required handle, and hard-stop on partial enumeration or access uncertainty.

findings.title: Nested static source metadata is not fully schema-closed
evidence: The static allowlist file itself is authenticated by an exact detached SHA-256 in the frozen draft.
The validator closes primary target and sentinel objects but does not fully close nested source_render and normalization objects.
Sentinel ID uniqueness is not independently asserted.
findings.adversarial_consequence: The exact frozen file is protected today, but a future regenerated allowlist could admit unreviewed nested metadata or ambiguous sentinel identifiers if the production loader relies on this validator alone.
findings.required_repair: Close every nested object, require exact sentinel ID and path-token uniqueness, and retain detached file-hash authentication.

preserved_dissent.reason: Even after these deterministic repairs, the precheck-to-rename and post-readback writer races remain unresolved.

next_action: Wait for both independent peer crosschecks, then obtain a fresh boss adjudication over all three reports. Preserve the frozen V3 draft as rejected evidence if any blocker is sustained, and implement repairs only in a newly named generation.
